analysis.one_liner: Axis Bank is India's third-largest private sector bank, lending to retail, SME and corporate customers and offering cards, wealth management and investment banking through its subsidiaries.
analysis.whats_happening: Axis Bank reported Q2 FY27 results on October 17, 2026: net profit rose 37.6% year-on-year to ₹7,003 crore, but this missed street estimates and the stock fell roughly 5% that day. Net interest margin (NIM) slipped to 3.36% (down 37 bps YoY, 10 bps QoQ) due to FCNR deposit costs, even as advances grew 23% YoY and asset quality kept improving (GNPA 1.16%, NNPA 0.35%). Management says Q2 likely marked the NIM cycle bottom and expects gradual improvement toward its 3.8% structural guidance from Q3 FY27 as repo-rate repricing flows through.
analysis.plain_terms: A bigger profit number does not always mean the core business got stronger. This quarter, Axis Bank's profit jumped 37.6%, but a large part of that came from setting aside far less money for bad loans (₹1,694 crore versus ₹3,547 crore a year ago) rather than from lending more profitably. Loans grew a healthy 23%, but the bank earned a slightly thinner margin on each rupee lent because of costlier foreign-currency deposits. That is the tension: the headline profit growth looks strong, but the market sold the stock off anyway because the underlying lending margin, not provisions, is what investors actually watch for durability.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): PAT ₹7,114 crore (+23% YoY), NII +8% YoY to ₹14,646 crore, NIM 3.46% - management called this the cycle low at the time. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): PAT ₹7,003 crore (+37.6% YoY) but missed street estimates, NII +12% YoY to ₹15,371 crore, core operating profit up only 11% YoY to ₹10,998 crore. NIM fell further to 3.36% (ex-FCNR impact it was 3.47%, actually up 1 bp sequentially) due to FCNR deposit mobilisation costs. The gap between 37.6% PAT growth and 11% core operating profit growth is explained almost entirely by provisions falling 52% YoY to ₹1,694 crore - a genuine but less repeatable source of profit growth than core lending income. One source (Univest) cited PAT of ₹7,704.67 crore for Q2, an outlier against the ₹7,003-7,005 crore figure converging across Business Standard, IndiaInfoline, Investing.com and Multibagg; the latter is treated as reliable and the outlier set aside.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock has returned 54.95% versus Nifty's 24.27% and peer Kotak Bank's 9.24% - a clear outperformance. Over 3 years it is roughly in line with Kotak (26.38% vs 25.47%) and ahead of Nifty (17.12%). Over 1 year it is roughly flat (+0.89%) but still beat both a falling Nifty (-11.43%) and a flat Kotak (+0.07%). The stock is currently 11.8% below its February 2026 peak of ₹1,401.92, trading near the middle of its 52-week range (₹1,160.41-₹1,401.92). The only corporate action on record is a 5:1 split in 2014, already reflected in the price series, with no demerger or spin-off to add back - so this drawdown is a genuine price correction tied to NIM worries and a results miss, not a crash caused by a corporate action.
analysis.valuation_read: Axis Bank trades around 13.7-14.4x trailing earnings and 1.7-1.9x book value (sources vary slightly by date), close to HDFC Bank's ~13.8x P/E and ~1.8x P/B, and a touch below the private banking sector's median P/E of ~14.9x. Why it looks reasonably priced rather than cheap: its ROE of ~14.2-14.5% is comparable to large peers, so the market isn't demanding a discount; whether it is actually cheap depends on whether the NIM-recovery story management is promising for H2 FY27 plays out - until then, this is a fairly priced bank, not a bargain.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently volume-led, not margin-led: advances grew 23% YoY and NII grew 12% YoY in Q2 FY27, while NIM compressed to 3.36% from higher levels a year ago because of costlier FCNR deposits. That is a less durable growth mix than volume-plus-margin expansion, though management argues the margin drag is temporary and should reverse as repo-linked loans reprice over H2 FY27.
analysis.health_read: Asset quality is genuinely improving and is not the concern here - GNPA fell to 1.16% (from 1.57% a year ago) and NNPA to 0.35% (from 0.45%), with slippages declining each quarter. The real question is financial risk on the funding side: Q2's reported profit growth leaned heavily on a 52% YoY drop in provisions rather than core operating profit (which grew only 11%), and NIM is still working through a cost-of-deposits squeeze. So credit risk looks well-controlled; margin/funding-cost risk is the live issue to watch.
analysis.ownership_read: LIC is the bank's legacy promoter-category holder with roughly 7.86-7.87% of shares, and none of it is pledged. Institutions (FIIs, DIIs, mutual funds) dominate the register at about 85.7%, with non-institutional holders at roughly 6.43%. There is no single marquee individual or star investor disclosed on the shareholding list - the base is institution-heavy rather than built around a well-known retail investor.
strengths: GNPA improved to 1.16% and NNPA to 0.35% in Q2 FY27, down from 1.57%/0.45% a year earlier
Advances grew 23% YoY and NII grew 12% YoY in Q2 FY27, showing real volume momentum
Zero promoter pledging on LIC's ~7.86% stake removes forced-selling risk from that holding
5-year shareholder return of 54.95% has comfortably beaten both the Nifty (24.27%) and peer Kotak Bank (9.24%)
watchpoints: NIM fell to 3.36% in Q2 FY27 (down 37 bps YoY) on FCNR deposit costs, and the stock fell ~5% on results day largely over this, not the profit headline
37.6% YoY PAT growth in Q2 FY27 was heavily aided by provisions falling 52% YoY (₹1,694 cr vs ₹3,547 cr); core operating profit grew just 11% YoY, a more modest underlying pace
Stock is 11.8% below its February 2026 peak of ₹1,401.92 and sits mid-range in its 52-week band
Valuation (~1.7-1.9x book, ~14x earnings) is in line with sector peers like HDFC Bank, so any re-rating depends on the promised NIM recovery actually showing up in Q3/Q4 FY27
analysis.one_thing: Whether NIM actually bottomed in Q2 FY27 and climbs toward management's 3.8% structural guidance over Q3-Q4 FY27 - the next couple of quarterly NIM prints will confirm or undercut that claim.
analysis.data_notes: PAT, NII, GNPA and NNPA figures for Q1 and Q2 FY27 were cross-checked across Business Standard, IndiaInfoline, Investing.com and Multibagg and converge closely; one outlier PAT figure (₹7,704.67 cr, Univest) was set aside. NIM breakdown and the FCNR-drag explanation came from fewer, more specialised sources (Investing.com, DSIJ, GuruFocus) so carries slightly less cross-verification. P/E and P/B multiples vary modestly by source and date (13.7-14.4x and 1.7-1.9x) - treat as an approximate range, not a precise figure; check exact current book value and EPS on Screener. Promoter/shareholding percentages (LIC ~7.86-7.87%, 0% pledge) converge across Trendlyne, Choice India and MarketsMojo. Not verified: segment-wise loan book mix, exact capital adequacy ratio for Q2 FY27 - check on Screener.
